title: DeepOrchid GPU reservoir qualification and isolation recap
text:
DeepOrchid GPU reservoir qualification and isolation recap

['From: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
To: elena.soto@deeporchid.ai, matt.chen@deeporchid.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: today’s discovery — isolation, burst, and 99th pct latency goals

Hi Elena / Matt —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap to make sure we’re aligned and to call out the concrete next steps we discussed on the call. I’ve tried to capture pain, goals, and our recommended path so we can move quickly to a technical deep-dive.

Pain points you emphasized:
- Tenant surface area: sensitive medical PII across customers, need strict cryptographic separation and audit trails.
- Unpredictable spikes from batch ingestion windows that drive up concurrency and tail latency.
- Cost sensitivity on steady-state but inability to tolerate noisy-neighbor interference.

High-level goals (what success looks like):
- Dedicated, isolated pool with hard tenancy boundaries and independent keying for PHI workload.
- 99th percentile generation latency < 150 ms at P95 traffic and graceful degradation at peak.
- Cost predictability: committed baseline with controlled burst for seasonal peaks.

Redwood recommended starting configuration (provisional, for qualification):
- Reserved pool: 8xA100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated to DeepOrchid), with burst capacity to 12x for up to 2 hours/day.
- Software isolation: tenant mapping + VPC-level network policies + customer-specific KV cache namespaces.
- Observability: per-tenant token-level cost and latency dashboards, 1s sampling for tails, and a scheduled 30-day quality/eval run.
- SLA target: 99.9% availability for the reserved pool; 99th pct latency SLO target: < 200 ms with plan to tune to 150 ms during ops ramp.

Immediate next steps we agreed on:
1) Technical workshop — 60–90 min deep-dive with your infra/ML infra folks (propose Thu 6/17).
2) Share the security/architecture questionnaire (we’ll populate and return in parallel).
3) Draft SOW and pricing sketch for 8 + burst (we’ll attach a first draft).
4) Procurement: you indicated a PO process of ~3 weeks once SOW is accepted; we’ll align calendar.

Attachments: deeporchid_requirements_v1.pdf — feel free to annotate; I’ll update the SOW from that.

If I missed anything or misstated priorities, call it out and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll schedule the tech workshop for Thu and loop in Rishi for the kernel/quantization discussion.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0198

Thanks Kim — this is great and captures our priorities. A few clarifications from my side:

- On isolation: we need tenant-level audit logs forwarded to our SIEM (Splunk) and a documented key rotation plan (we use customer-managed KMS).
- Latency SLO: the 150 ms 99th is aspirational — we must start with a defensible baseline (your 200 ms suggestion is acceptable for pricing).
- Burst behavior: burst can’t be used for PHI writes unless the burst nodes are under the same KMS policies; we’ll need that constraint written in the SOW.

We can do Thu 6/17 11:00–12:30 PT for the technical workshop. Attendees from DeepOrchid: me, Matt Chen (platform lead), and our infra engineer Priya Rao.

I’ll upload an annotated version of the requirements PDF later today. Please include the draft SOW in the Drive link you mentioned so our legal/procurement has visibility.

— Elena
VP Product & Ops, DeepOrchid AI

Looping in a few technical notes ahead of Thu’s workshop:

- Kernel/execution: based on Elena’s expected seq lengths (~1k tokens typical, up to 2k for some workloads) we should propose a quantized 8-bit path for steady-state and an FP16 path for burst to maintain tail latency.
- Cache strategy: per-tenant KV namespaces with strict eviction TTLs to avoid cross-tenant leakage. We should spell out the namespace mapping in the SOW appendix.
- Autoscaling/burst: recommend a policy of vertical burst (add GPUs to pool) with pre-warmed images and warm-up traffic gating for the first 10 minutes of a burst window to prevent one-off cold-start tail spikes.

I’ll prepare a short ops checklist and a proposed monitoring dashboard (Grafana / token-level traces) to share before the workshop.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
